seoTitle: Free Inflation Calculator: Future Cost of Money
metaDescription: See what an amount will cost after years of constant inflation, and how much purchasing power it loses. Free inflation calculator, runs in your browser.
intro: Enter an amount, an annual inflation rate and a number of years. The tool shows the future cost, the equivalent value today and the purchasing power lost.
why: Prices drift upwards, and a sum that looks comfortable now buys less every year. That matters when you plan a pension, set a savings target, agree a multi-year contract or ask for a pay rise. The calculation is simple compounding, but few people do it in their heads for a ten or twenty year span. This tool shows both directions: what something that costs 1,000 now might cost later, and what 1,000 received later is worth in current prices. It also states the share of purchasing power lost. It assumes a single constant rate, which real inflation is not, so treat it as a scenario tool. It runs locally in your browser.
howTo: Enter the expected inflation rate per year and the number of years.
Read the future cost, the value in current terms and the purchasing power lost.

faq.q: What formula does the calculator use?
faq.a: Future cost equals the amount times (1 plus the rate) to the power of the years. Dividing by the same factor gives what a future amount is worth in current prices.

faq.q: Does it use real historical inflation data?
faq.a: No. It applies the constant rate you type and does not fetch consumer price indices. For past periods, use the official inflation figures from your national statistics office.

faq.q: Why does purchasing power fall by less than the rate times years?
faq.a: Because the effect compounds. At 3% for 10 years, prices rise about 34%, but purchasing power falls by about 25.6%, since the loss is measured against the higher future price.

faq.q: Can I enter a negative rate for deflation?
faq.a: Yes, a negative number is accepted. The future cost then falls and purchasing power rises. The years value can also be fractional.
